title: Ablative Armor — Editor Intro
summary: Opening splash turns the damaged thermal panel into a mass-and-material problem: survival in flight costs weight, and the obvious aerospace solution is no longer readily available.
panelPlan: Full-page opening/title splash around the damaged nose/heat-shield section on the Launch-Shop work deck. Pair scorched material with a physical mass ledger and empty or crossed-out supply slots for unavailable aerospace shielding.
Make the rocket hardware beautiful but used: this is an engineering object that survived enough to expose the next limit, not wreckage.
Do not show the decommissioned furnace, salvaged refractory, tile geometry, attachment redesign, thermal-test results, Rhonda's detention or any later Issue 7 event.
Use the sequence SPEED → HEAT → MASS as the visual rhythm, then open the final lines into the issue title.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Getting through the sky is not the same as surviving it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Heat turns elegant materials into very expensive smoke.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And every kilogram of protection is a kilogram that cannot be fuel, payload or reserve.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The obvious answer is aerospace shielding.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tethergrid has made the obvious answer difficult to buy.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Good thing Launch-Shop has never been especially attached to obvious answers.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic opening title page. Preserve exact caption text. It should make the thermal problem feel large and tactile without revealing where replacement material comes from or how the crew ultimately solves attachment, manufacturing or testing.
